summary: In 2004 British mercenary Simon Mann and wealthy backers plotted to overthrow Equatorial Guinea's dictator Teodoro Obiang to seize its oil wealth; the bungled plot ended with arrests in Zimbabwe and torture in Black Beach Prison.

evidence.note: long segment on Mad Mike Hoare's Congo campaigns and the 1981 Seychelles coup attempt
Macias terror campaign kills or drives out a third of the population; stadium mass execution
Obiang ousts his uncle in 1979 and runs an oil-funded kleptocracy
Mann's birth in 1952, Eton, Sandhurst and SAS service covered
Executive Outcomes fights UNITA in Angola's civil war, later the RUF in Sierra Leone
2003 meeting with Ely Calil starts the coup plot
difficulty of sourcing arms; bribery deal with Zimbabwe Defence Industries
Mann's force arrested at Harare in 2004, advance team held in Equatorial Guinea
extradition to Black Beach, torture, pardon in 2009 and release

notes: Wonga Coup and Simon Mann both primary: Part 1 is background (Haggard, Hoare, Denard, Forsyth's 1973 plot, Macias and Obiang); Part 2 is Mann's life and the plot. Haggard's novel treated as framing, so covered_span starts at Mann's birth. Mann believed alive. Forsyth's 1973 plot gets a real segment but the five-subject limit left him in keywords.
